purpose: WP05.9 controlled budget scaling of the WP05.8 beta=0.5 arm: the same 15 complete beta=0.5 round-2 DAgger shards (52,500 decisions, labels verified byte-identical to the 5k conversion), the same mix / optimiser / training seed / model / dev suite, but 20,000 steps instead of 5,000 (2,560,000 samples). It tests whether the replicated 0/20 dev result is still explained by training budget, or whether it is an action-collapse / state-coverage limit that extra steps do not fix. The 20 dev episodes are descriptive only: this is not G410-2 and no gate is evaluated

budget_explanation.question: does the 0/20 dev result at 20,000 steps still look like a training-budget limitation, or is it an action-collapse / policy-quality limit that more budget does not fix?
budget_explanation.short_answer: training budget no longer explains 0/20. Going from 5,000 to 20,000 steps (4x samples) cut the train loss from 0.6586 to 0.3245 and raised macro-recall from 0.2733 to 0.5904 (x2.16), reaching DAgger-window top1 0.9926 / macro-recall 0.9703, yet dev clears stayed 0/20 and mean survival moved only +25.55 frames (+1.51 %). The policy is not collapsed onto one action (18-bin histogram, id 0 ('idle') holds 0.6087, entropy 1.8660 of 4.1699 bits, 12.45 distinct actions per episode); the remaining limit is state coverage from a single DAgger round plus a persistent passive/idle bias

offline_budget_evidence.curve_note: window_loss_last_500 is the mean of the per-100-step block losses in the last 500 steps before the mark; cumulative_loss is the sample-weighted mean over all blocks up to the mark (it equals metrics.loss at 20,000)

stream_epochs.note: at 20,000 steps the same 46,397 S1 rows and 52,500 DAgger rows are replayed many times, so extra budget buys repetition, not new states

survival_ceiling.note: not one of 20 dev episodes reached even a quarter of the cap

action_collapse_evidence.verdict: no collapse to a single action: the pooled 18-bin histogram keeps 12.45 distinct actions per episode and 1.8660 bits of entropy (max 4.1699); but the distribution stays skewed to passive play -- idle (focus 0 + move 0) is 0.6087 of decisions and the east/west directions take most of the rest. 4x budget widened the repertoire only slightly (12.5 -> 12.45 actions per episode) and moved idle by -1.97 pp

budget_explanation.conclusion: 0/20 is replicated at 20,000 steps, so it is not an undertraining artefact of the 1,000- or 5,000-step budgets. The budget axis is exhausted for dev: 4x steps bought a 1.5 % survival gain and no clears, while the same 4x cut the offline loss in half and more than doubled macro-recall. The binding constraints left are (a) state coverage -- one DAgger round of 52,500 decisions replayed ~40x cannot represent the states the policy itself visits, and (b) a persistent idle/passive action bias at decision time. More steps over the same rows are not the lever; a new collection round or a different objective (e.g. penalising idle, or on-policy correction) would be, and both are out of scope for WP05.9
what_would_settle_it: a second DAgger collection round (new on-policy states) is out of scope for WP05.9: no data was collected here and this run does not authorise it

an offline held-out check on different seeds would separate 'memorised the train batches' from 'generalises'; the DAgger-window top1 of 0.9926 strongly suggests memorisation, which in-sample train metrics cannot by themselves distinguish
a training-seed sweep (seeds 1-2) would give a variance estimate; one seed cannot separate a poor seed from a poor recipe
an explicit action-distribution diagnostic (idle penalty / entropy bonus) would test whether the passive bias, rather than the state coverage, is the first thing to break

offline_vs_dev_gap.what_it_shows: between 5,000 and 20,000 steps the offline fit improves enormously while dev survival barely moves: the step budget is no longer the binding constraint on dev

offline_5k_to_20k.note: by the last 500 steps the model reproduces the teacher's chosen action on the collected DAgger rows almost perfectly (top1 0.9926, macro-recall 0.9703), i.e. 4x budget bought memorisation of the same 52,500 rows

offline_vs_dev_gap.interpretation: the divergence is the point: loss halved (x2.03) and macro-recall x2.16 while mean dev survival moved +25.55 frames (+1.51 %) and clears stayed at 0/20. Extra steps over the same single DAgger round perfect the imitation on collected states without teaching the policy what to do on its own states, where it still idles most of the time

comparison.rule: descriptive side-by-side only. The three beta=0.5 arms share the same 15 shards, the same 52,500 converted label rows (verified byte-identical), the same mix, optimiser, training seed 0, model and 20 dev seeds, so the only controlled change is the step budget 1,000 -> 5,000 -> 20,000. The beta=1.0 arm differs in the injection coefficient and is not a controlled budget comparison. No interval, no significance test, no gate, no decision rule
confounds: one training seed (0) and one checkpoint per arm: no variance estimate
the 20k run reuses the 52,500 rows ~40 times (DAgger stream epochs 40) and 46,397 S1 rows 12 times, so the extra budget is repetition of the same states, not new coverage
the beta=1.0 50k arm used injection_rate 1.0 while the beta=0.5 shards used injection_rate 0.500857, so that contrast is descriptive only
offline metrics are in-sample train-batch metrics, not held-out accuracy
20k trained on an otherwise idle host; the 1k and 5k arms shared the host with a G410-1 teacher batch, so throughput/wall-clock is not comparable even though the samples/s differ by ~1.6x
the dev episodes are the 20 dev seeds only; G410-2 is not measured and no pass/fail threshold is defined or implied

scope.purpose: WP05.9 controlled budget scaling: B0 behaviour cloning on the same 15 complete beta=0.5 round-2 DAgger shards, 20,000 steps instead of 5,000, plus the 20 descriptive dev episodes
scope.game_launched_note: only by tools/rl/v410_student_eval.py for the 20 dev episodes; no collection rollout was run

not_claimed: this is NOT G410-2: no confirm seeds were run and no gate is evaluated
this is NOT a pass rate, a development score, or a four-arm comparison verdict
the 20 dev episodes are descriptive only; no interval or significance test is attached
no data was collected, no new DAgger round was run, and no shard was regenerated
the offline metrics are in-sample train-batch metrics, not held-out accuracy
a single 0/20 at 20,000 steps does not prove the approach is dead, only that more steps over the same 52,500 rows do not clear stage 0
the beta=1.0 contrast in this file is descriptive; that arm is not a controlled budget comparison
limits: one arm (B0), one training seed (0), one budget triple (1k/5k/20k): no variance estimate, so budget cannot be fully separated from seed noise
52,500 round-2 decisions from a single DAgger round; at 20,000 steps the DAgger stream is replayed ~40x and the S1 stream 12x, so the extra budget is repetition rather than new state coverage
in-sample train metrics; there is no held-out offline evaluation
dev episodes are the 20 dev seeds only (1000-1019); G410-2 is not measured
wall time and samples/s are not comparable with the 1k/5k arms, which ran while a G410-1 teacher batch shared the 20-core host; the 20k run had the host to itself

the two nvidia-smi lines in run_train.sh and run_eval.sh logged a format error (a dropped trailing character in the driver scripts); both drivers exited 0 and GPU evidence therefore comes from the train_run.json gpu block, not from the log header
